rows.section: Personal income tax (tulumaks)
rows.basis: Taxable income of a resident individual, per year
rows.note: One flat rate on the income of resident individuals. The basic exemption (€700 a month, €8,400 a year) is deducted first; from 2026 it no longer falls as income rises. Employers withhold 22% from pay. The planned 2% security tax was not introduced.
rows.source_title: Maksu- ja Tolliamet: Maksumäärad ja maksuvaba tulu suurus, 2026 (last updated 26.03.2026); Maksumuudatused 2026. aastal (27.11.2025)

rows.section: Basic exemption (maksuvaba tulu) and deductions
rows.label: Basic exemption, per month
rows.note: The deductions are claimed on the annual return (the 2026 return is filed from 15 February 2027).
rows.source_title: Maksu- ja Tolliamet: Maksuvaba tulu arvestamine (last updated 25.05.2026); Maksumäärad ja maksuvaba tulu suurus, 2026 (last updated 26.03.2026)

rows.section: Basic exemption (maksuvaba tulu) and deductions
rows.label: Income-based phase-out (the 'tax hump', maksuküür)
rows.value: Abolished from 1 January 2026: the full amount applies at any income (2025: up to €654 a month or €7,848 a year, falling as income rose)
rows.note: The deductions are claimed on the annual return (the 2026 return is filed from 15 February 2027).

rows.section: Basic exemption (maksuvaba tulu) and deductions
rows.label: How it is applied
rows.value: On a written application to one employer or payer only (Income Tax Act § 42(2)); the Social Insurance Board applies it to pensions automatically
rows.note: The deductions are claimed on the annual return (the 2026 return is filed from 15 February 2027).

rows.section: Employee contributions: unemployment insurance and funded pension
rows.label: Who pays the funded pension
rows.value: Second pillar members; joining is compulsory for people born in 1983 or later, who may later apply to stop contributions
rows.note: Employees pay no social tax: the 33% social tax is the employer's. Income tax (22%) is withheld from pay after the basic exemption.
rows.source_title: Pensionikeskus: Rejoining the second pillar after a 5-year break; Changing the rate of contributions to 2%, 4% or 6%; Exemption from contributions to II pillar; Mandatory funded pension

rows.section: Employee contributions: unemployment insurance and funded pension
rows.label: Changing the funded-pension rate
rows.value: Application to Pensionikeskus by 30 November; the new rate applies from 1 January and can be changed once a year
rows.note: Employees pay no social tax: the 33% social tax is the employer's. Income tax (22%) is withheld from pay after the basic exemption.
rows.source_title: Pensionikeskus: Rejoining the second pillar after a 5-year break; Changing the rate of contributions to 2%, 4% or 6%; Exemption from contributions to II pillar; Mandatory funded pension

rows.section: Employee contributions: unemployment insurance and funded pension
rows.label: Stopping and rejoining
rows.value: Contributions can be stopped or the savings withdrawn; from 2026 a member can rejoin after a 5-year break (previously 10 years)
rows.note: Employees pay no social tax: the 33% social tax is the employer's. Income tax (22%) is withheld from pay after the basic exemption.
rows.source_title: Pensionikeskus: Rejoining the second pillar after a 5-year break; Changing the rate of contributions to 2%, 4% or 6%; Exemption from contributions to II pillar; Mandatory funded pension

rows.section: Sole proprietors (FIE): income tax and social tax
rows.label: Income tax on business income after allowed deductions
rows.note: Business income is declared once a year (form E with the annual return, by 30 April); the Tax and Customs Board then sets the final social tax, due by 1 October. Retired and studying sole proprietors pay no advances or annual minimum, only 33% of actual profit.

rows.value: 22% on business income after allowed deductions; social tax 33% on the same income

rows.section: Freelancers, the self-employed and new residents
rows.label: Inbound or expat tax regime
rows.value: None: residents are taxed on worldwide income at 22% with the normal basic exemption; there is no reduced rate or exemption for new residents
rows.note: Self-employed figures are the 2026 amounts published by the Tax and Customs Board (EMTA); the visa rules are in the Aliens Act § 62^5 and Interior Minister regulation no. 82.
rows.source_title: Maksu- ja Tolliamet: Residentsuse määramine (last updated 23.10.2026)

rows.section: Freelancers, the self-employed and new residents
rows.label: Tax residency
rows.value: A permanent home in Estonia or at least 183 days in Estonia within 12 consecutive months
rows.note: Self-employed figures are the 2026 amounts published by the Tax and Customs Board (EMTA); the visa rules are in the Aliens Act § 62^5 and Interior Minister regulation no. 82.
rows.source_title: Maksu- ja Tolliamet: Residentsuse määramine (last updated 23.10.2026)

rows.section: Freelancers, the self-employed and new residents
rows.label: Digital-nomad visa (viisa kaugtöö tegemiseks)
rows.value: A short-stay (C) or long-stay (D) visa for remote work for a foreign employer, the applicant's own foreign company or mainly foreign clients; a D visa allows up to 365 days within 12 months
rows.note: Self-employed figures are the 2026 amounts published by the Tax and Customs Board (EMTA); the visa rules are in the Aliens Act § 62^5 and Interior Minister regulation no. 82.
rows.source_title: Riigi Teataja: Siseministri määrus nr 82 'Pikaajalise viisa andmise, viibimisaja vormistamise ja viibimisaja pikendamise kord ja tähtajad ning piisavate rahaliste vahendite määr' (version in force from 22.05.2026), § 15 lg 7; Välismaalaste seadus § 62^5; 2026. aasta riigieelarve seadus § 2 lg 5 p 5; Politsei- ja Piirivalveamet: Long-term visa

rows.section: Freelancers, the self-employed and new residents
rows.label: Digital-nomad visa: sufficient funds per day in Estonia (0.6 × the €220 monthly subsistence level)
rows.note: from 1 January 2026; legal income for the six months before applying must also be documented
rows.source_title: Riigi Teataja: Siseministri määrus nr 82 'Pikaajalise viisa andmise, viibimisaja vormistamise ja viibimisaja pikendamise kord ja tähtajad ning piisavate rahaliste vahendite määr' (version in force from 22.05.2026), § 15 lg 7; Välismaalaste seadus § 62^5; 2026. aasta riigieelarve seadus § 2 lg 5 p 5; Politsei- ja Piirivalveamet: Long-term visa

rows.section: Freelancers, the self-employed and new residents
rows.label: Digital-nomad visa: tax
rows.value: More than 183 days in Estonia within 12 consecutive months makes the holder an Estonian tax resident
rows.note: Self-employed figures are the 2026 amounts published by the Tax and Customs Board (EMTA); the visa rules are in the Aliens Act § 62^5 and Interior Minister regulation no. 82.

rows.section: Freelancers, the self-employed and new residents
rows.label: Where to apply
rows.value: An Estonian representation abroad that handles visas, or a Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) service office in Estonia
rows.note: Self-employed figures are the 2026 amounts published by the Tax and Customs Board (EMTA); the visa rules are in the Aliens Act § 62^5 and Interior Minister regulation no. 82.

rows.section: Freelancers, the self-employed and new residents
rows.label: e-Residency
rows.value: A government digital ID for running an Estonian company online; it is not tax residency, citizenship, a residence permit, a visa or a right to enter Estonia
rows.note: Self-employed figures are the 2026 amounts published by the Tax and Customs Board (EMTA); the visa rules are in the Aliens Act § 62^5 and Interior Minister regulation no. 82.
